title: Revised hydrogeologic framework of the Floridan aquifer system in Florida and parts of Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina
citation: Williams, L.J., and Kuniansky, E.L., 2015, Revised hydrogeologic framework of the Floridan aquifer system in Florida and parts of Georgia, Alabama, and South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1807, map scale 1:5,000,000.
notes:
Packet 1 is plates 1-14 (well location map, correlation chart, contour and isopach maps, cross sections A-A' to H-H'). Contour labels on plates 3-6 are scattered map-face text and were not attributed to lines. Only section G-G' (plate 13) starts in South Carolina; its SC well BFT-2055 was read from page-image tiles (contacts sampled from the PDF at the well column; elevations in ft relative to NGVD 29, inferred). Wells in Georgia, Alabama and Florida on plates 7-14 were not recorded. Units are recorded from the report text in later packets, not from the correlation chart.
Packet 2 holds plates 15-23 (cross sections I-I' to Q-Q', all in Florida; no values taken) and the front matter, abstract and introduction. Vertical datum of the report is NGVD 29 (p. 36).
Packet 3 (pages 41-60): introduction, methods, salinity mapping, stratigraphy and structure. Mostly about Florida and Georgia; recorded the South Carolina-relevant items (Beaufort arch, leaky middle unit in coastal Georgia and South Carolina). The correlation chart (fig. 4) columns were not attributed to units because column alignment is lost in the text.
Packet 4 (pages 61-79): stratigraphy, permeability, marker horizons, upper confining unit, intermediate and Brunswick aquifer systems, top of the Floridan aquifer system. Recorded South Carolina items; Florida and Georgia site details not recorded. Hydraulic conductivities of the offshore Hilton Head/Tybee cores are given as a range in the text, not per sample site.
Packet 5 (pages 80-103): top and base of the system, thickness, Upper Floridan aquifer zones. Recorded South Carolina items only; Florida and Georgia test-site details not recorded.
Packet 6 (pages 104-127): Upper Floridan aquifer zones, middle composite units (table 7), Lower Floridan aquifer. Recorded South Carolina and adjacent Savannah-area items; Florida test sites not recorded. Figure 36 is a reduced copy of plate 13 (read in packet 1).
Packet 7 (pages 128-153): hydraulic properties, transmissivity (table 13), groundwater flow and pumpage. Recorded the South Carolina county rows of table 13 (county statistics of aquifer tests, not per site, so stored as groundwater properties rather than water tests). Transmissivity values are rounded to two significant digits per the table footnote. Rows for Alabama, Florida and Georgia not recorded.
Packet 8 (pages 154-174): groundwater flow, pumpage (table 15, percent of permitted wells by county; not recorded), salinity, summary, and references A-Pr. Only references relevant to South Carolina geology and hydrogeology were recorded; the many Florida and Georgia site reports were skipped.
Packet 9 (pages 175-179): references Re-Y and back matter. Only references relevant to South Carolina were recorded; Florida and Georgia site reports skipped.
